set.t: Private lakeshore at Robinson Lake: permission needed. Benton Lake (national forest campground) is look-only. The pin is on the 1880 shingle-mill site at Robinson (Big) Lake, about 6 mi NE of Fremont, which fits the 1926 account's lumber-village lake; today's Benton Lake, 14 mi NNE ('Blue L.' on the 1900 atlas, with no village or mill), carries only the modern legend's name.
set.pl: Shingle-mill site, SE shore of Robinson Lake, Sherman Twp (1880 atlas); the 1926 telling's lake; modern legend says Benton Lake
pinev: 1880 Newaygo County atlas (archive.org 3927793), Sherman Twp T13N R13W leaf 43: Wetzel Bros. steam shingle mill on the SE shore of Robinson (Big) Lake, S sec 10; Worcester Sta. (sec 15) and Alleyton (sec 1) nearby. Robinson Lake (43.532,-85.854) is ~6 mi NE of Fremont, matching the 1926 account.
Today's Benton Lake (GNIS, Huron-Manistee NF, 43.671,-85.888), 14 mi NNE, was 'Blue L.' in 1900 and is only the modern legend's name.

src: Atlas of Newaygo County (1880), Sherman Twp T13N R13W (archive.org 3927793, leaf 43)

set.st: Herman Rechenberg spent four years spading his late father's farm. In January 1924, digging cellar dirt for his chickens, he struck a glass jar holding about $1,300 in mildewed bills, which he banked at the Produce Exchange Bank, St Paul. He found it on Thursday 17 January 1924: $1,360 in mildewed bills. His father, 48 years on the homestead from about 1864, had died about 1912 apparently without money even for his burial. The 1910 and 1920 censuses put Anton and Herman Rechenberg in Mendota Twp (today's Mendota Heights), not West St Paul; the 1916 Dakota atlas shows no Rechenberg on the Mendota plate, so the parcel awaits the 1928 plat.
set.n: Rechenberg's jar of mildewed bills, Dodd Road farm, Mendota Heights (found 1924)
set.pl: Dodd Road, Mendota Twp (Mendota Heights), Dakota Co; parcel pending the 1928 plat
pinev: 1910 and 1920 US census: Anton and Herman Rechenberg in Mendota Twp, Dakota Co; pin on Dodd Road in the township, r2 km, parcel not placed.

pinev: Hunters' dugout on the SW point (Dodge 1970, after Harman 1929); his earlier cabin, elsewhere on the island, burned c.1900. SW tip read from the USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM island outline (tip ~44.4777,-84.7307); ring covers the SW lobe.
1880 census: James and John Flynn in Gerrish Twp, likely the source of the island's name.
